design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 1 (homesite_reservation_holds), frozen 2026-10-17 11:15 EDT.

[Step 0 — draw and scope] draw_counts.py --task 1 -> {"prerequisite_problems": 2, "factor_counts": [4, 4, 5]}. Occupied by task 0: homesite_ext_activation_hold_term, homesite_ext_extension_fee_charge, homesite_ext_extended_hold_term and their three tools. Claimed here (disjoint): homesite_ext_release_premium_refund (4 factors), homesite_ext_reinstatement_fee_charge (4), homesite_ext_reinstated_hold_term (5, root); tools sign_homesite_release_13bc71ff (user — the blueprint's own customer act, the buyer's signed release), record_reinstatement_fee_fa042025 (agent — the desk records a phone payment, per the blueprint), reinstate_homesite_hold_f9d4ebfd (agent). Difficulty coverage after this task: all six extended policies, every policy claimed exactly once.
Decisions: the release tool books the release with its triggered refunds (homesite_released triggers homesite_refund_issued in the charter) and the premium-fee share Calloway keeps, as the lines of the signed Release and Settlement, so no settlement obligation is left after the release; the full-refund-window gate is replaced by a declared overwrite (window starts on the later of the reservation date and the funds-complete day), which retires that base gate; the reinstated hold is passed as whole days and written as today + days.

[Why a good test] Priya only asks to have LM-0158 back on hold. The agent must learn from the reinstatement rule that a lapsed hold is not reinstated while another of her reservations stands held (BC-0171), have her sign that release with a correctly computed premium refund (1,380.88; 119.12 kept), take a reinstatement fee computed through discount, a combined surcharge and a reminder-lateness method (55.25), and only then fix a reinstated term that depends on how that fee was paid (12 days).

[Problem tree] root homesite_ext_reinstated_hold_term. Edge A state_gate/state form (negated): 'A lapsed hold is not reinstated until no other reservation of the buyer stands in pending deposit or held status.' Only the buyer's release write in this difficulty moves another reservation of hers out of held. False at opening: BC-0171 status held. Edge B value_input/state form (affirmative): 'The reinstated hold term is fixed only after a reinstatement fee payment for the lapsed hold stands on the reservation ledger.' Only the reinstatement-fee payment tool writes a reinstatement_fee component. False at opening: LM-0158 ledger has no reinstatement_fee row. Order: release, fee, reinstatement (release and fee commute: disjoint reservations, hashed ids). Deletion sensitivity: skip fee -> hold_days 9 (check_compute value_input test confirms change); skip release -> BC-0171 stays held, no settlement rows. Persona never names either prerequisite.

[Base-invariant card] Release: release_refund (window gate retired by declared overwrite), expiry_reinstatement / lot_swap / builder_withdrawal / conversion scope only; deposit refunded in full is inherited. Fee: returned_payment.cure_window bound to the empty source receipt (no return on LM-0158). Reinstatement: agg_community_premium_cap.portfolio_room — after the release she holds only LM-0158 (Corner, not premium) -> room; expiry_reinstatement.reinstatement_window — expired 2026-10-15, counted days 10-16..10-18 inclusive, 2026-10-17 inside; just-fails 2026-10-19. Overwrites: expiry_reinstatement fee clause, expiry_reinstatement 'A reinstated hold runs extension_days ...', release_refund window sentence and after-window percent sentence.

[Business-object card] LM-0158 (3f961bbf-...): deposit 1,000.00 card RCPT-LM-11807 + 500.00 ACH RCPT-LM-11822 (part card), convenience fee 27.50 (near-miss: not deposit), reminder 2026-10-14 (late by two days). BC-0171 (6d00e3ee-...): deposit 5,000.00 wire RCPT-BC-12264, premium 1,500.00 ACH RCPT-BC-12279 (sets the window start 2026-10-09; near-miss: counting from the reservation date gives 4 days after the window, the same grace tier here, but the rule anchors on the later day). Cross-category: purchase BC-0109 closed, outside_lender; warranty HomeCare 1-3-10 Plus, original_buyer, active. Both seeded holds' hold expiry dates are what the activation policy of this charter yields (16 and 17 days), so history teaches no contrary rule.

[Factor card — release (expected 1,380.88, baseline 750.00)] loyalty percent (warranty original/active 75, multi-source) baseline 50 -> 1,182.35; lender bonus (outside_lender +5) baseline 0 -> 1,341.18; grace bonus (3 days after window, +5) baseline 0 -> 1,341.18; forfeit method (no extension: prorate 9/17, half up) baseline whole -> 1,275.00. 85% -> 1,275.00 share, forfeit 225.00 x 9/17 = 119.12, refund 1,380.88.
[Factor card — reinstatement fee (expected 55.25, baseline 100.00)] lender discount 15% -> 65.00 under baseline; card surcharge part 5% -> 53.13; timing second day 25% -> 44.63; reminder method late -> halved rounded up, baseline 110.50. 100 x 0.85 = 85.00 -> x1.30 = 110.50 -> 55.25.
[Factor card — reinstated term (expected 12, baseline 7)] base length by fee method (ach -> 10) baseline 7 -> 9; lapse add-back (late reminder: half of 2 rounded up = 1) baseline 0 -> 11; loyalty bonus (3) baseline 0 -> 9; card shortening (part, 1) baseline 0 -> 13; letter shortening (37 days, 1) baseline 0 -> 13.

[Persona] Warm, flustered relocating engineer; volunteers only the goal and phone; BC-0171 and her home only if asked; conditional: releases BC-0171 once told it blocks the reinstatement, pays the fee by ACH by phone, closes on the new last day.

[Standard solution] find_customers -> verify(phone, DOB) -> reservations -> ledger -> warranty -> purchase -> unlock_user + user signs release (R'=BC-0171, RCPT-BC-12264 5000.00, RCPT-BC-12279 1380.88 / 119.12, original_method) -> unlock+call fee (55.25, ach, '') -> unlock+call reinstate (hold_days 12, reinstatements_used 1).
[Verification run] check_compute --task 1: '1.json 3 13 4 9 41 12 True' / COMPUTE OK; replay_tasks --task 1: REPLAY OK (closure 11 = init 11); check_solvability, check_grounding, check_cross_fire, check_extended, check_task_tools --task 1: OK.
[Draft recomputation from visible context] The published reinstatement rule names the waited-on states; the reservations finder shows BC-0171 held and no reinstatement_fee row; the release and fee rules plus ledger, warranty and purchase records give 1,380.88 / 119.12 / 55.25 / 12 with no second reading (the only free order — release vs fee — commutes).

[Round 2 rework — policy-task audit]
- T1-1 (release computation had no near-miss): seeded a second purchase agreement for Priya, BC-0127 in Brookstone Crossing, Heritage Collection, signed 2020-06-12 and cancelled 2020-07-10 when her Calloway Home Mortgage loan fell through (status cancelled, financing calloway_home_mortgage, nothing held or owed). A careless reader taking it for the lender tier gets +10 points (release refund 1,420.59 instead of 1,380.88) and a 40% reinstatement discount; the rules count only an agreement that 'stands closed'. The persona mentions it only when asked about her other Calloway records. Scored values unchanged (recomputed).
- DG-2 (base 'Days are counted from the day after the reservation date ...' undeclared): declared in homesite_ext_release_premium_refund.overwrite, replaced_by 'Days are counted from the day after the window start, and a release received on the last counted day is inside the window.'
- O-9: the inside-window full refund now carries 'where premium_fee_refundable_within_window is true' in rule, baseline and compute. O-1: 'that half rounded half up to the cent' stated in the rule and ladder. O-6: the 'courtesy for a buyer committed to a single homesite' clause removed from the reinstated-term rule. O-10/O-11/O-12/O-13: kept as observations (both reinstatement conditions necessary; lapse add-back reads as an anchor; card factors keyed on chargeback exposure; third forfeit tier unreachable for premium classes but part of the general ladder). T1-O1: lapse anchored on end_date per base.
user_scenario: You are Priya Chandrasekar, a software engineer who has just accepted a job in Denver. You already own a Calloway home in Brookstone Crossing in Fuquay-Varina, North Carolina. You are warm and talkative, a bit flustered, and you apologize for having let something slip while you were traveling for the job interviews. On a house-hunting trip you reserved homesite LM-0158 in Larkspur Meadows in Castle Rock, Colorado, and you just saw that its hold ran out on Thursday while you were busy. You want LM-0158 back, put on hold for you again today, because that is the lot you want now that you are moving to Colorado. That is what you are calling about, and you are happy for the representative to take care of it on their end. To find you, you give your cell number, 9195550113. When asked to confirm your identity you give your date of birth, 1985-11-02; if they need another item, your ZIP code is 27526, your email is priya.chandrasekar@gmail.com and the last four of your Social is 2391. You don't bring up any of your other Calloway records on your own. If the representative asks, you confirm you also put a hold on homesite BC-0171 in Brookstone Crossing a little over a week ago, when you still thought you might stay in North Carolina, and that you own your current Calloway home in Brookstone Crossing, which you bought new with a loan from your credit union; before that, in 2020, you had signed for a different Brookstone lot with a Calloway Home Mortgage loan but cancelled that agreement when the loan fell through. If the representative explains that LM-0158 cannot be put back on hold while you still hold another homesite, you decide right away to let Brookstone BC-0171 go, since you are moving to Colorado anyway; when they hand you the release in your buyer portal, you sign it, entering exactly the reservation, receipt numbers, amounts and refund choice they read to you, and you accept the settlement as they explain it. You don't know the refund rules and never suggest figures. If the representative tells you there is a fee to put LM-0158 back on hold, you ask them to take it by bank transfer from your checking account over the phone, in the amount they state. Once the representative tells you LM-0158 is on hold for you again and gives you its new last day, you thank them, say you'll start on the purchase agreement next week, and end the call without asking for anything else.

edges.condition: Every homesite_reservations row of the buyer other than the expired one stands in status converted, released, expired or withdrawn; none stands in pending_deposit or held.
edges.policy_source: A lapsed hold is not reinstated until no other reservation of the buyer stands in pending deposit or held status.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: Her Brookstone Crossing reservation BC-0171 stands held at 2026-10-17.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Her signed release sets BC-0171 to released (end date 2026-10-17); no other reservation of hers is pending or held.

edges.condition: A homesite_events row of event_type homesite_payment_received with deposit_component reinstatement_fee stands on the expired reservation.
edges.policy_source: The reinstated hold term is fixed only after a reinstatement fee payment for the lapsed hold stands on the reservation ledger.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: LM-0158's ledger holds two reservation_deposit payments, a card convenience fee and a notice; no reinstatement_fee payment.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The 55.25 ACH reinstatement_fee payment posts; fee_paid_by reads ach and the reinstated base length becomes 10 instead of 7.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The release (BC-0171) and the fee payment (LM-0158) write disjoint rows on different reservations; the release refund reads only BC-0171 and the fee reads only LM-0158, and both row ids are hashed from their own arguments, so either order gives the same terminal state and the same values (1,380.88 and 55.25); the reinstatement follows both.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Without the release BC-0171 stays held (terminal status held instead of released, no refund/retained rows), so the state the reinstatement waits on never holds.

Without the fee payment fee_paid_by is empty, the base length falls to extension_days 7 and hold_days becomes 9 instead of 12 (hold expiry 2026-10-26 instead of 2026-10-29); the 55.25 row is also missing.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario asks only to have LM-0158 back on hold. BC-0171 is mentioned only if the representative asks, its release only after the representative explains it blocks the reinstatement, and the fee only after the representative states it. No prerequisite policy id appears.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: sign_homesite_release_13bc71ff, record_reinstatement_fee_fa042025 and reinstate_homesite_hold_f9d4ebfd perform ctx.update/ctx.create with the passed values only; reinstate_homesite_hold_f9d4ebfd sets status held even while another reservation of the buyer is held and with no fee payment, raising nothing.
